title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Let U = U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,∞} over Q. S_3 acts on U by permuting the three punctures, and Grothendieck considers the quotient stack (U_{0,3,Q}, S_3). On the next page he names it M'_{1,1,Q}; it is the j-line stack with the generic ±1 removed. Let π̄ be the geometric profinite fundamental group of U, which is free profinite on x, y, z with xyz = 1. Set M = H_1(U(C), Z) ≅ Z^2. As an S_3-module, M = Z^3/Z(1,1,1), the permutation module on the punctures modulo the diagonal. Its completion is M̂ = π̄^ab = M ⊗ Ẑ, with Galois acting through the cyclotomic character, so M̂ ≅ M ⊗ Ẑ(1).

The arithmetic fundamental group of the stack, divided by [π̄, π̄], is an extension of Γ = Γ_Q × S_3 by M̂. On the previous page Grothendieck notes that the Fermat tower shows this extension is split, i.e. it is a semidirect product.

The question. Classify splittings up to M̂-conjugacy. These form a torsor under H^1(Γ, M̂).

The argument.
- Hochschild–Serre (inflation–restriction) with normal subgroup S_3 gives (294): 0 → H^1(Γ_Q, H^0(S_3, M̂)) → H^1(Γ, M̂) → H^0(Γ_Q, H^1(S_3, M̂)).
- Since S_3 is finite and M is finitely generated, H^i(S_3, M̂) = H^i(S_3, M) ⊗ Ẑ.
- Earlier he had shown that the discrete extension of S_3 by M (from the topological fundamental group of the orbifold) is split, with any two splittings conjugate by a unique element of M. That is exactly H^1(S_3, M) = 0 and H^0(S_3, M) = 0, which is (296).
- Direct check: from 0 → Z → Z^3 → M → 0 we get H^0(S_3, M) = 0. Also H^1(S_3, M) = ker(H^2(S_3, Z) → H^2(S_2, Z)). This map is Z/2 → Z/2 restricted to a transposition, which is injective, so the kernel is 0.
- Hence both ends of (294) vanish, giving (297): H^1(Π_Q × S_3, M̂) = 0. Together with H^0(Γ, M̂) = 0, the S_3-equivariant splitting is unique up to conjugation by a unique element.

Geometric translation (the Theorem). There is a pro-étale cover U_∞ of the stack (U_{0,3,Q}, S_3) whose pullback to U_{0,3,Q̄}, forgetting the S_3-action, is the universal (maximal) abelian pro-cover. Any two such covers are related by a unique isomorphism.
- Existence comes two ways: from the Fermat tower, and from the general theory of §49 VI. Uniqueness then shows the two constructions agree, which was the conjecture stated on the previous page.
- The point stressed on the next page: without the S_3-action, the obstruction H^1(Γ_Q, M̂) ≅ M ⊗ (Q^*)^ is huge, so there are many Kummer-type twists of the tower. The S_3-rigidity kills everything, with no input about Γ_Q at all.
errors: Writing (U_{0,3,Q}, S_3) = M_{1,1,Q} on this page is imprecise. The quotient stack is M_{1,1} with the generic μ_2 removed (the rigidification), not M_{1,1} itself. Grothendieck corrects this himself to M'_{1,1,Q} on the next page.
The page notation switches between Γ_Q (previous page) and Π_Q (in (297)) for Gal(Q̄/Q). This is harmless.
Strictly, H^1 = 0 only gives uniqueness of the splitting up to conjugacy. A 'unique isomorphism' also needs H^0(Γ, M̂) = 0, which holds by (296)/(295) and is implicit in the text.
The second line of (296) is just the first line tensored with Ẑ (valid since S_3 is finite and M is finitely generated). Fine, but it is not a separate fact.

ideas.what: Vanishing of H^0 and H^1 of S_3 with coefficients in H_1(P^1 - 3 points) = Z^3/diagonal
ideas.modern_name: group cohomology of the reduced permutation module; rigidity of the orbifold extension

ideas.what: Inflation–restriction for Γ_Q × S_3 acting on the abelianized geometric π_1, giving H^1(Γ_Q × S_3, π̄^ab) = 0
ideas.modern_name: Hochschild–Serre five-term sequence; classification of sections of the metabelian quotient of the arithmetic fundamental group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hochschild–Serre (method); application standard in anabelian/Galois–Teichmüller literature

ideas.what: Canonical S_3-equivariant Q-model of the maximal abelian pro-cover of P^1 - {0,1,∞}, unique up to unique isomorphism, realized by the Fermat tower
ideas.modern_name: Fermat tower as canonical model of the maximal abelian cover; rational structure on the metabelian quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (Annals 1986, Fermat tower and Galois action on metabelian π_1); Anderson; Anderson–Ihara (1988)

ideas.what: Using the S_3-symmetry (equivalently passing to the stack M'_{1,1}) to rigidify descent data and kill the twisting ambiguity H^1(Γ_Q, M̂) ≅ M ⊗ (Q^*)^
ideas.modern_name: equivariant descent / rigidification of fields of definition by automorphism groups

missed.claim: An explicit uniqueness statement: the universal abelian pro-cover of P^1 - {0,1,∞}_{Q̄} has a unique S_3-equivariant descent to Q, unique up to unique isomorphism. Uniqueness follows purely from H^0 = H^1 = 0 for S_3 on H_1, with no input from Γ_Q. Hence the Fermat tower is the canonical such model. This is a small but clean observation. The Fermat tower's role is well known (Ihara, Anderson), but the S_3-rigidity formulation on M'_{1,1} is rarely stated this way.
missed.quote: la relation triomphale (297) H^1(Π_Q × S_3, M̂) = 0 ! ... Théorème Il existe un revêtement profini U_∞ de (U_{0,3 Q}, S_3) = M'_{1,1 Q}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a canonical normalization of the metabelian (Ihara/Anderson) Galois representation on the stack M'_{1,1}. This is relevant to choosing canonical tangential base points or descent data in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory. Most likely already implicit in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct and elegant, but a routine group-cohomology computation. The underlying object (the Fermat tower as Q-model of the maximal abelian cover) is well known from Ihara and Anderson. The S_3-rigidity remark is a nice unpublished detail, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'L'image inverse U_∞ de U_∞ dans U_{0,3 Q̄} (oubli op. de S_3)': read as the inverse image \overline{U_∞} of U_∞ in U_{0,3,Q̄}, 'oubli de l'op. de S_3' (forgetting the S_3-action).
'est "le" revêtement absolu universel' should probably read 'revêtement abélien universel'. M is the abelianization, so the universal abelian cover is meant.
The insertion above the line reads '= M'_{1,1 Q}' (with a prime), matching the next page, rather than '= M_{1,1 Q}'.
'l'extension S^+/μ_S de S_3 par M' refers to the (discrete) orbifold extension studied earlier; the symbols are uncertain in the handwriting.
'ô nouveau contre tout attente' should read 'ô nouveau — contre toute attente, je l'avoue !'
